study.question: Which auxiliary task group supplies the useful product-branch context updates: cart/fav, buy, or their combination? In g0-r0043, product-only AUC=0.6684156159937658, residual-only=0.6676246607842132, both=0.6684573078909239, neither=0.6678548720585206. Product-only is just 0.00004169 below the incumbent but 0.00056074 above neither. This isolates a consequential remaining ownership uncertainty without adding architecture capacity. Does selective task-conditioned transfer improve on product-all and the incumbent, or is joint transfer needed?
study.hypothesis: Complementary cart/fav and buy supervision through the signed product branch produces better shared context embeddings than either group alone at identical forward capacity. This is a provisional route-complementarity hypothesis, not an established mechanism. The earlier additive-adapter g0-r0033 study had all=0.6670575100016033, cart/fav=0.6668914773504744, buy=0.6666426317152966, none=0.6668051956575413, an interaction=0.00032860. Both selective implementations underperformed all there; the later signed product has a different Jacobian and was absent from that comparison, so those results cannot establish product-specific task complementarity.

study.proposed_difference: Add aux_product_context_tasks as a fixed list of task names. During auxiliary training only, detach the product context input when its task is excluded. Fixed-state forward values, capacity, learned modules, buffers and RNG are unchanged; task modules continue to learn even when their context embedding input is detached. This is a diagnostic refinement of an inherited model, not a new unified architecture or an originality claim.
predictions: Integrity bridges: product_all_bridge must reproduce g0-r0043-branch_product_only (AUC0.6684156159937658), and product_none_bridge must reproduce g0-r0043-branch_neither_bridge (AUC0.6678548720585206), under the same frozen seed/recipe. They are reproduction checks, not extra seeds.

Primary provisional prediction: A_all > A_cartfav and A_all > A_buy, and A_all > A_none. The predeclared AUC interaction I=A_all-A_cartfav-A_buy+A_none is positive. Report both main effects in both strata of the other factor rather than only I.

Alternative useful outcome: a selective candidate exceeds product_all_bridge and incumbent g0-r0039-context_product (0.668457307890924), with lower logloss and no added parameters. That would falsify the complementarity prediction but motivate task-selective transfer as a preliminary candidate.

The prior product-only versus neither improvement was concentrated in history17_64 and history_gt64; use frozen bins empty/1_16/17_64/gt64 to diagnose whether task-group changes occur in the same region. This new slice prediction is prospective; earlier slice selection was exploratory.

If A_all does not exceed both selective groups, the stated useful complementarity prediction is unsupported for this implementation. I<=0 rejects the predicted positive AUC interaction; positive I alone is insufficient without useful main effects.

No selective candidate above incumbent and product-all means no new performance improvement, even if group effects localize a training route. A small single-seed increment cannot establish generalization or semantic mechanism.

If a gain disappears under later admissible paired repetitions or is explained by gradient magnitude, optimizer accumulation, or validation selection, revise the route-complementarity explanation. The current factorial cannot exclude these alternatives.
